name: CommonCatalog
description: A dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images with synthetic captions generated using BLIP-2, designed for training text-to-image diffusion models. The dataset contains roughly 70 million non-commercial CC images, of which approximately 25 million can be used commercially.

creator.name: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov

citeAs: Gokaslan, A., Cooper, A. F., Collins, J., Seguin, L., Jacobson, A., Patel, M., Frankle, J., Stephenson, C., & Kuleshov, V. (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825v1 [cs.CV]
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was sourced from the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs. Images were re-scraped from Flickr based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata to obtain high-resolution versions (exceeding 4K resolution). Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The remaining images were divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) categories.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the YFCC100M dataset, which contains Flickr IDs linking to original data. The images were re-scraped from Flickr to obtain very high resolution versions (exceeding 4K).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for the captioning process. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded from the dataset. The remaining images were filtered into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) categories based on their Creative Commons licenses. Images were re-scraped from Flickr to obtain high-resolution versions. For captioning, images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 pixels.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. BLIP-2 consists of three components: a pre-trained, frozen visual encoder, a learned transformer network that converts visual embeddings into a text prompt, and a frozen large language model (LLM) that takes in the prompt. The model was chosen based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. All YFCC100M Creative-Commons images were captioned using this approach, requiring about 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2 captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions. LAION-2B captions often contain product names, irrelevant details, or poor grammar and syntax. Quantitatively, BLIP-2 captions are higher quality than ground-truth captions in terms of CLIP Score, at the cost of caption diversity. A reduction in diversity of n-grams was observed in synthetic captions, with a decrease in unique trigrams.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The commercial (CommonCatalog-C) and non-commercial (CommonCatalog-NC) CC-image and synthetic-caption datasets are released on HuggingFace with associated data cards. BLIP-2 captions for non-derivative (ND) CC images are also released as an evaluation set.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses copyright concerns by using only Creative-Commons-licensed images with known provenance that expressly allow for copying, adaptation, and commercial use. This approach avoids the unclear provenance issues associated with web-scraped datasets like LAION-5B. The use of synthetic captions via telephoning provides a 'lossy compression' that does not literally resemble the original images, potentially reducing copyright concerns.
rai:dataBiases: The model underperformed in several categories including faces, general photography, and paintings. These categories originated from the Conceptual Captions dataset, which relies on web-scraped data. The YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. The model is less likely to generate iconic characters given suggestive prompts compared to SD2.
rai:dataLimitations: CC images rarely have the alt-text captions necessary to train text-to-image models; those that do have associated text often just include the image title or a URL. Only roughly 70 million usable CC images could be found, which is significantly less than the billions of images in LAION. The dataset is about a decade old and not as current as LAION-2B. The model underperformed in categories like faces, general photography, and paintings. Reduced diversity of n-grams in synthetic captions was observed.
rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image latent diffusion models. The dataset is intended for training high-quality text-to-image generative models while addressing copyright concerns. Users could supplement with their own datasets (e.g., FFHQ) if they seek to fine-tune models for specific categories like faces.
